title: (Windows) Creating or trying to open a file named 'com1' will always fail
body:
### Tested versions

Godot v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8142) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

Attempting to create a file named 'com1' with any extension, anywhere in the FileSystem docker will fail. If you externally create or manually rename a file to com1, the engine will fail to open it.

Appears to be a case of tripping over Windows' reserved filenames, as per [here](https://help.interfaceware.com/v6/windows-reserved-file-names): this bug also occurs with 'com2' etc down that list

This appears to be intended behavior to dodge the reserved filenames, but a clearer error message or explanation would be preferred; I'd thought there was possibly something wrong with my resource IDs until I raised it on the discord.

### Steps to reproduce

In any project, attempt to create a resource or text file named 'com1', 'com2' etc, with any extension. It will fail.

If a file named 'com1' is manually renamed or externally added to the project, again with any extension, the editor will refuse to open it with `ERROR: editor/editor_node.cpp:1536 - Condition "res.is_null()" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_OPEN`

For the MRP, open the project and attempt to open com1.txt via the FileSystem docker

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[com-bug-project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23395585/com-bug-project.zip)
